description:
pkix-ct/Cargo.toml:13-36, pkix-ct/src/lib.rs:42-64

Four features add or remove public items:

- `std`: enables `std::error::Error` impl on `Error`
- `ocsp`: enables `sct_list_from_ocsp_response`
- `log-list`: enables `CtLog`, `CtLogList`, `SctVerifier`,
  `merkle_*`, `MerkleAuditPath`, `SignedTreeHead`
- `log-list-json`: enables `CtLogList::from_google_log_list_json`,
  implies `log-list`

The doc comment in `lib.rs:42-64` shows `mod log_list` /
`mod verify` gated on `log-list`; `verify` is the largest module
(1359 lines, includes the verifier, Merkle helpers, and STH).

A caller wanting just SCT parsing (zero CT verification, just
extract the SCTs from a TLS extension or OCSP response) needs only
the default+`ocsp` features. A caller wanting SCT verification
without log_list.json ingestion needs `log-list` without
`log-list-json`. A caller wanting the full surface needs
`log-list-json` (which transitively pulls `log-list`).

Three contract problems:

1. The `log-list` feature gates a LOT of unrelated functionality
   — Merkle inclusion proofs (`verify_inclusion`, `MerkleAuditPath`),
   STH signature verification (`verify_sth`, `SignedTreeHead`), and
   SCT signature verification (`SctVerifier::verify_*`) all live
   behind `log-list`. None of them strictly need the log list to
   work as data structures; they only need it to look up keys at
   verify time. The feature name is misleading — `log-list` reads
   as "log list parsing" but it actually gates "anything that
   touches CT log keys".

2. Inverse: a caller wanting Merkle inclusion proof verification
   only (against a root_hash they trust through some other
   channel — e.g. a witness signature) gets dragged into the
   full `log-list` feature including the `BTreeMap` and `sha2`
   dep, even though Merkle inclusion is pure hash math with no
   log-list dependency.

3. The `log-list-json` implies `log-list` is documented in Cargo.toml
   but the inverse (what `log-list` gives you BEFORE adding
   `log-list-json`) is not stated in the public API docs. A caller
   reading the rustdoc has no way to know that `SctVerifier` is
   available with `log-list` alone, vs. `log-list-json`.

Recommendation:

- Split `log-list` into three features: `log-list` (just CtLog +
  CtLogList), `verify` (SctVerifier + STH verification, depends
  on log-list), `merkle` (verify_inclusion + MerkleAuditPath,
  no deps).

- Document the public-surface-by-feature in the crate-level rustdoc
  with a table:

  | Feature       | Public items added              |
  |---------------|---------------------------------|
  | (none)        | Error, SCT parser types, TLS ext|
  | ocsp          | OCSP-response extractor         |
  | log-list      | CtLog, CtLogList                |
  | verify        | SctVerifier + STH               |
  | merkle        | verify_inclusion, audit path    |
  | log-list-json | from_google_log_list_json       |

Priority P3 because the feature shape is internal-ish and can be
re-split non-breakingly (renaming features IS breaking; adding new
features is not, so add new feature aliases first, deprecate the
broad `log-list`).
title: Features change public surface but feature interaction undocumented — log-list-json implies log-list, but other combinations not stated
